LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Put 給 before the person who receives the action: 我給她寫信. A negative or modal word goes before 給.

items.question: Where does 給 go in the book’s pattern?
items.answer: Both 我給她寫信 and 我寫信給她 are correct. The book’s pattern puts 給 before the receiver: 我給她寫信. Do not split it as 我寫信給寫她.

right.english: I write a letter to her.

items.question: Is it 給 or 跟 for “with a friend”?
items.answer: Use 跟 for “with”: 我跟朋友一起去. 給 marks the receiver of an action.

right.english: I go with a friend.

items.question: Where does the receiver go in 哥哥沒給我打電話?
items.answer: After 給: 哥哥沒給我打電話. Do not put the receiver after the verb.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Arrange a first step, a wait, and the next step.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: Use 先 for the first step, 等 for the condition you wait for, and 再 for the step after it. Without 先, 等…再… still means “wait until…, then…”.

lessonWorld.title: Plan what happens next
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei needs to decide, wait for a free time, and then arrange the meeting.
lessonWorld.traditional: 先決定，等朋友有空，再約時間。
lessonWorld.simplified: 先决定，等朋友有空，再约时间。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Xiān juédìng, děng péngyǒu yǒukòng, zài yuē shíjiān.
lessonWorld.english: Decide first, wait until the friend is free, then arrange a time.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: 先 + first step，等 + condition，再 + next step

items.question: Is the “then” word 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then, later” in a sequence. 在 is “at” or “happening now”: 我們晚上再去。

right.english: We will go in the evening.

items.question: What comes first: 等 or the action it waits for?
items.answer: 等 comes before the condition: 等她起床了，你再跟她說. Do not put 再 before 等.

right.traditional: 等她起床了，你再跟她說。
right.pinyin: Děng tā qǐchuáng le, nǐ zài gēn tā shuō.
right.english: Wait until she gets up, then tell her.
right.simplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.wrongSimplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.question: Where does 先 go in 先…等…再…?
items.answer: 先 comes before the first action: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯.
items.wrongTraditional: 你做功課先，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。

right.traditional: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
right.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
right.english: Do your homework first, and when Dad is back home, we will have dinner together.
right.simplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

items.wrongSimplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

text.traditional: 這家餐廳今天人太多了，我們以後再來吧。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅今天人太多了，我们以后再来吧。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jīntiān rén tài duō le, wǒmen yǐhòu zài lái ba.
text.english: This restaurant is too crowded today; let’s come again later.

text.traditional: A：爸爸，這個句子是什麼意思？B：我現在沒空，晚上再告訴你。
text.simplified: A：爸爸，这个句子是什么意思？B：我现在没空，晚上再告诉你。
text.pinyin: A: Bàba, zhège jùzi shì shénme yìsi? B: Wǒ xiànzài méi kòng, wǎnshang zài gàosu nǐ.
text.english: A: Dad, what does this sentence mean? B: I have no time now; I will tell you tonight.

text.traditional: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一點兒累，我們週末再去吧。
text.simplified: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一点儿累，我们周末再去吧。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào bu yào gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù dǎqiú? B: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu yìdiǎnr lèi, wǒmen zhōumò zài qù ba.
text.english: A: Do you want to play ball with me? B: I am a little tired today; let’s go this weekend.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再去外面。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再去外面。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài qù wàimiàn.
text.english: It is too cold; wait until the bus comes, then we will go outside.

text.traditional: A：妳決定買這種茶了嗎？B：等我先生也喝了，我們再決定買不買。
text.simplified: A：你决定买这种茶了吗？B：等我先生也喝了，我们再决定买不买。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ juédìng mǎi zhè zhǒng chá le ma? B: Děng wǒ xiānsheng yě hē le, wǒmen zài juédìng mǎi bu mǎi.
text.english: A: Have you decided to buy this kind of tea? B: Wait until my husband has also tried it; then we will decide whether to buy it.

text.traditional: A：這個問題很難，你可以教我嗎？B：我現在要去上課，等下課了再教你，好不好？
text.simplified: A：这个问题很难，你可以教我吗？B：我现在要去上课，等下课了再教你，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Zhège wèntí hěn nán, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma? B: Wǒ xiànzài yào qù shàngkè, děng xiàkè le zài jiāo nǐ, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: This question is hard; can you teach me? B: I am going to class now; I will teach you after class, okay?

text.traditional: A：我們一起去吃飯吧。B：現在去吃飯的人太多了，我想先寫功課，等人少了再去吃。
text.simplified: A：我们一起去吃饭吧。B：现在去吃饭的人太多了，我想先写功课，等人少了再去吃。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù chīfàn ba. B: Xiànzài qù chīfàn de rén tài duō le, wǒ xiǎng xiān xiě gōngkè, děng rén shǎo le zài qù chī.
text.english: A: Let’s eat together. B: Too many people are eating now; I want to do my homework first, then eat when there are fewer people.

text.traditional: A：現在太熱了！B：對啊，我們先去吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩，好不好？
text.simplified: A：现在太热了！B：对啊，我们先去吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Xiànzài tài rè le! B: Duì a, wǒmen xiān qù chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: It is too hot now! B: Right; let’s eat ice cream first, then go to the beach when it is not hot, okay?

text.traditional: 媽媽：明天妳打算去哪裡？女兒：我要先去朋友家，等百貨公司開了，再去買衣服。
text.simplified: 妈妈：明天你打算去哪里？女儿：我要先去朋友家，等百货公司开了，再去买衣服。
text.pinyin: Māma: Míngtiān nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ? Nǚ’ér: Wǒ yào xiān qù péngyǒu jiā, děng bǎihuò gōngsī kāi le, zài qù mǎi yīfu.
text.english: Mother: Where do you plan to go tomorrow? Daughter: I will go to my friend’s place first, then buy clothes when the department store opens.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: Say that an action is completed, with or without a quantity.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Put 了 after the verb or verb-object to show the action is completed. With a quantity, one 了 reports a finished past action; a second 了 at the end says “so far, and maybe more.”

items.question: Where does 了 go with a quantity — after the verb or after the object?
items.answer: In this past-action sentence, put 了 after the verb, before the quantity: 我喝了兩杯咖啡. Without 了 before the quantity, the sentence has a different (change-of-state) meaning.

right.pinyin: Wǒ hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi.
right.english: I drank two cups of coffee.

items.question: What does a second 了 add?
items.answer: One 了 reports a finished past action. The final 了 says “so far”: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了 means two cups so far, and more may follow.

right.traditional: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了。
right.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi le.
right.english: I have already drunk two cups of coffee (so far).
right.simplified: 我已经喝了两杯咖啡了。

items.wrongSimplified: 我已经喝了两杯咖啡了。

items.question: Does 沒 take 了 in a simple past negative?
items.answer: No. 他沒來 means he did not come. 他沒來了 would mean “he is no longer coming”, a different change-of-state meaning.

right.english: He did not come.

text.traditional: 他已經去上課了。
text.simplified: 他已经去上课了。
text.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng qù shàngkè le.
text.english: He has already gone to class.

text.traditional: 我今天早上去看醫生了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上去看医生了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang qù kàn yīshēng le.
text.english: I went to see the doctor this morning.

text.traditional: 我跟弟弟都寫功課了。
text.simplified: 我跟弟弟都写功课了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn dìdi dōu xiě gōngkè le.
text.english: My younger brother and I both did our homework.

text.traditional: 我上個禮拜學了十個中國字。
text.simplified: 我上个礼拜学了十个中国字。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng ge lǐbài xué le shí ge Zhōngguó zì.
text.english: I learned ten Chinese characters last week.

text.traditional: 我已經學了四百多個中國字了。
text.simplified: 我已经学了四百多个中国字了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng xué le sìbǎi duō ge Zhōngguó zì le.
text.english: I have already learned more than four hundred Chinese characters.

text.traditional: 爸爸上個月買了一輛新車。
text.simplified: 爸爸上个月买了一辆新车。
text.pinyin: Bàba shàng ge yuè mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē.
text.english: Dad bought a new car last month.

text.traditional: 爸爸已經買了一輛新車了，還想再買一輛。
text.simplified: 爸爸已经买了一辆新车了，还想再买一辆。
text.pinyin: Bàba yǐjīng mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē le, hái xiǎng zài mǎi yí liàng.
text.english: Dad has already bought a new car, and he still wants to buy another one.

text.traditional: 他昨天晚上吃了兩個蘋果。
text.simplified: 他昨天晚上吃了两个苹果。
text.pinyin: Tā zuótiān wǎnshang chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ.
text.english: He ate two apples last night.

text.traditional: 他很愛吃蘋果，已經吃了一個了，還想再吃。
text.simplified: 他很爱吃苹果，已经吃了一个了，还想再吃。
text.pinyin: Tā hěn ài chī píngguǒ, yǐjīng chī le yí ge le, hái xiǎng zài chī.
text.english: He loves apples; he has already eaten one and wants another.

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.titleEnglish: Emphasize One Past Detail with 是…的
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Ask or say when, where, who, or how a past action happened.
LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Put 是 before the detail you want to emphasize and 的 at the end. 是 is optional in a positive sentence, but it cannot be left out in a negative sentence.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen knows that Youmei met someone. She wants the missing detail.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

LESSON_ELEVEN_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: Subject + 是 + focus + action + 的

patternRows.english: When did they go back to their countries?
It was yesterday they went back to their countries.
Where did you come from?
It was school where I came from.
Whom did you go shopping with?
It was my classmate whom I went shopping with.
How did you meet him?
It was through the internet that I met him.

items.question: In 是…的, does the sentence end with 了 or 的?
items.answer: Use 的 to close the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天來的. 了 is not the ending here.

right.english: It was yesterday that he came.

items.question: Can I leave out 是 in a negative sentence?
items.answer: No. 是 cannot be left out in a negative sentence: 他不是開車來的.

right.pinyin: Tā bú shì kāichē lái de.
right.english: He did not come by car.

items.question: Where does 的 go?
items.answer: At the end of the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天到的. Do not drop it after the verb.

right.english: It was yesterday that he arrived.

text.traditional: A：他已經到學校了。B：他是幾點到的？A：他是三點三十分到的。
text.simplified: A：他已经到学校了。B：他是几点到的？A：他是三点三十分到的。
text.pinyin: A: Tā yǐjīng dào xuéxiào le. B: Tā shì jǐ diǎn dào de? A: Tā shì sān diǎn sānshí fēn dào de.

text.traditional: A：張先生來了。B：他是開車來的嗎？A：不是，他是走路來的。
text.simplified: A：张先生来了。B：他是开车来的吗？A：不是，他是走路来的。
text.pinyin: A: Zhāng xiānsheng lái le. B: Tā shì kāichē lái de ma? A: Bú shì, tā shì zǒulù lái de.
text.english: A: Mr. Zhang has come. B: Did he come by car? A: No, he came on foot.

text.traditional: A：你的中文說得真好，你是在哪裡學的？B：我在台灣學的。
text.simplified: A：你的中文说得真好，你是在哪里学的？B：我在台湾学的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ de Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn hǎo, nǐ shì zài nǎlǐ xué de? B: Wǒ zài Táiwān xué de.
text.english: A: Your Chinese is really good; where did you learn it? B: I learned it in Taiwan.

text.traditional: A：你知道她的手機號碼嗎？是誰告訴你的？B：是她媽媽告訴我的。
text.simplified: A：你知道她的手机号码吗？是谁告诉你的？B：是她妈妈告诉我的。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ zhīdào tā de shǒujī hàomǎ ma? Shì shéi gàosu nǐ de? B: Shì tā māma gàosu wǒ de.
text.english: A: Do you know her phone number? Who told you? B: Her mother told me.

text.traditional: 他是昨天晚上到的，不是今天早上到的。
text.simplified: 他是昨天晚上到的，不是今天早上到的。
text.pinyin: Tā shì zuótiān wǎnshang dào de, bú shì jīntiān zǎoshang dào de.
text.english: It was last night that he arrived, not this morning.

items.question: Where does 了 go with a quantity — after the verb or after the object?
items.answer: In this past-action sentence, put 了 after the verb, before the quantity: 我喝了兩杯咖啡. Without 了 before the quantity, the sentence has a different (change-of-state) meaning.

right.pinyin: Wǒ hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi.
right.english: I drank two cups of coffee.

items.question: What does a second 了 add?
items.answer: One 了 reports a finished past action. The final 了 says “so far”: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了 means two cups so far, and more may follow.

right.traditional: 我已經喝了兩杯咖啡了。
right.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng hē le liǎng bēi kāfēi le.
right.english: I have already drunk two cups of coffee (so far).
right.simplified: 我已经喝了两杯咖啡了。

items.wrongSimplified: 我已经喝了两杯咖啡了。

items.question: Does 沒 take 了 in a simple past negative?
items.answer: No. 他沒來 means he did not come. 他沒來了 would mean “he is no longer coming”, a different change-of-state meaning.

right.english: He did not come.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 是 + focus + action + 的

patternRows.english: When did they go back to their countries?
It was yesterday they went back to their countries.
Where did you come from?
It was school where I came from.
Whom did you go shopping with?

How did you meet him?

items.question: In 是…的, does the sentence end with 了 or 的?
items.answer: Use 的 to close the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天來的. 了 is not the ending here.

right.english: It was yesterday that he came.

items.question: Can I leave out 是 in a negative sentence?
items.answer: No. 是 cannot be left out in a negative sentence: 他不是開車來的.

right.pinyin: Tā bú shì kāichē lái de.
right.english: He did not come by car.

items.question: Where does 的 go?
items.answer: At the end of the emphasized past detail: 他是昨天到的. Do not drop it after the verb.

right.english: It was yesterday that he arrived.

text.english: It is for a new friend. Look, this is a card from him.

text.traditional: 他寫的字真好看。你們是怎麼認識的？
text.simplified: 他写的字真好看。你们是怎么认识的？
text.pinyin: Tā xiě de zì zhēn hǎokàn. Nǐmen shì zěnme rènshi de?

text.simplified: 我们是上网认识的，我看到他写的文章，然后留言问了他一个问题，他回答得很有趣。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Arrange a first step, a wait, and the next step.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 先 for the first step, 等 for the condition you wait for, and 再 for the step after it. Without 先, 等…再… still means “wait until…, then…”.

lessonWorld.title: Plan what happens next
lessonWorld.prompt: Youmei needs to decide, wait for a free time, and then arrange the meeting.
lessonWorld.traditional: 先決定，等朋友有空，再約時間。
lessonWorld.simplified: 先决定，等朋友有空，再约时间。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Xiān juédìng, děng péngyǒu yǒukòng, zài yuē shíjiān.
lessonWorld.english: Decide first, wait until the friend is free, then arrange a time.

grammarPages.pattern: 先 + first step，等 + condition，再 + next step

items.question: Is the “then” word 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then, later” in a sequence. 在 is “at” or “happening now”: 我們晚上再去。

right.english: We will go in the evening.

items.question: What comes first: 等 or the action it waits for?
items.answer: 等 comes before the condition: 等她起床了，你再跟她說. Do not put 再 before 等.

right.traditional: 等她起床了，你再跟她說。
right.pinyin: Děng tā qǐchuáng le, nǐ zài gēn tā shuō.
right.english: Wait until she gets up, then tell her.
right.simplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.wrongSimplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。

items.question: Where does 先 go in 先…等…再…?
items.answer: 先 comes before the first action: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯.
items.wrongTraditional: 你做功課先，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。

right.traditional: 你先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
right.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
right.english: Do your homework first, and when Dad is back home, we will have dinner together.
right.simplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

items.wrongSimplified: 你先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。

text.traditional: 這家餐廳今天人太多了，我們以後再來吧。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅今天人太多了，我们以后再来吧。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jīntiān rén tài duō le, wǒmen yǐhòu zài lái ba.
text.english: This restaurant is too crowded today; let’s come again later.

text.traditional: A：爸爸，這個句子是什麼意思？B：我現在沒空，晚上再告訴你。
text.simplified: A：爸爸，这个句子是什么意思？B：我现在没空，晚上再告诉你。
text.pinyin: A: Bàba, zhège jùzi shì shénme yìsi? B: Wǒ xiànzài méi kòng, wǎnshang zài gàosu nǐ.
text.english: A: Dad, what does this sentence mean? B: I have no time now; I will tell you tonight.

text.traditional: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一點兒累，我們週末再去吧。
text.simplified: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？B：我今天有一点儿累，我们周末再去吧。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào bu yào gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù dǎqiú? B: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu yìdiǎnr lèi, wǒmen zhōumò zài qù ba.
text.english: A: Do you want to play ball with me? B: I am a little tired today; let’s go this weekend.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再去外面。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再去外面。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài qù wàimiàn.
text.english: It is too cold; wait until the bus comes, then we will go outside.

text.traditional: A：妳決定買這種茶了嗎？B：等我先生也喝了，我們再決定買不買。
text.simplified: A：你决定买这种茶了吗？B：等我先生也喝了，我们再决定买不买。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ juédìng mǎi zhè zhǒng chá le ma? B: Děng wǒ xiānsheng yě hē le, wǒmen zài juédìng mǎi bu mǎi.
text.english: A: Have you decided to buy this kind of tea? B: Wait until my husband has also tried it; then we will decide whether to buy it.

text.traditional: A：這個問題很難，你可以教我嗎？B：我現在要去上課，等下課了再教你，好不好？
text.simplified: A：这个问题很难，你可以教我吗？B：我现在要去上课，等下课了再教你，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Zhège wèntí hěn nán, nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma? B: Wǒ xiànzài yào qù shàngkè, děng xiàkè le zài jiāo nǐ, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: This question is hard; can you teach me? B: I am going to class now; I will teach you after class, okay?

text.traditional: A：我們一起去吃飯吧。B：現在去吃飯的人太多了，我想先寫功課，等人少了再去吃。
text.simplified: A：我们一起去吃饭吧。B：现在去吃饭的人太多了，我想先写功课，等人少了再去吃。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù chīfàn ba. B: Xiànzài qù chīfàn de rén tài duō le, wǒ xiǎng xiān xiě gōngkè, děng rén shǎo le zài qù chī.
text.english: A: Let’s eat together. B: Too many people are eating now; I want to do my homework first, then eat when there are fewer people.

text.traditional: A：現在太熱了！B：對啊，我們先去吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩，好不好？
text.simplified: A：现在太热了！B：对啊，我们先去吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩，好不好？
text.pinyin: A: Xiànzài tài rè le! B: Duì a, wǒmen xiān qù chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán, hǎo bu hǎo?
text.english: A: It is too hot now! B: Right; let’s eat ice cream first, then go to the beach when it is not hot, okay?

text.traditional: 媽媽：明天妳打算去哪裡？女兒：我要先去朋友家，等百貨公司開了，再去買衣服。
text.simplified: 妈妈：明天你打算去哪里？女儿：我要先去朋友家，等百货公司开了，再去买衣服。
text.pinyin: Māma: Míngtiān nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ? Nǚ’ér: Wǒ yào xiān qù péngyǒu jiā, děng bǎihuò gōngsī kāi le, zài qù mǎi yīfu.
text.english: Mother: Where do you plan to go tomorrow? Daughter: I will go to my friend’s place first, then buy clothes when the department store opens.

grammarPages.explanation: Put 給 before the person who receives the action: 我給她寫信. A negative or modal word goes before 給.

My older brother did not make a phone call to me.

items.question: Where does 給 go in the book’s pattern?
items.answer: Both 我給她寫信 and 我寫信給她 are correct. The book’s pattern puts 給 before the receiver: 我給她寫信. Do not split it as 我寫信給寫她.

right.english: I write a letter to her.

items.question: Is it 給 or 跟 for “with a friend”?
items.answer: Use 跟 for “with”: 我跟朋友一起去. 給 marks the receiver of an action.

right.english: I go with a friend.

items.question: Where does the receiver go in 哥哥沒給我打電話?
items.answer: After 給: 哥哥沒給我打電話. Do not put the receiver after the verb.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

text.english: A: Haven’t you written a birthday card to your older brother yet? B: Not yet; I will write it tonight.

dialogue.setting: 在教室裡 · In the classroom

text.traditional: 妳跟那位新朋友見面了沒有？
text.simplified: 你跟那位新朋友见面了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ gēn nà wèi xīn péngyǒu jiànmiàn le méiyǒu?
text.english: Have you met up with your new friend yet?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
text.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: I haven’t decided to meet him or not.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？
text.simplified: 你担心什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ dānxīn shénme?
text.english: What are you worried about?

text.traditional: 我有點兒緊張，我以前沒有這種經驗，所以覺得這樣有點兒奇怪。
text.simplified: 我有点儿紧张，我以前没有这种经验，所以觉得这样有点儿奇怪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǐqián méiyǒu zhè zhǒng jīngyàn, suǒyǐ juéde zhèyàng yǒudiǎnr qíguài.
text.english: I am a little nervous. I have never had an experience like this before, so I think it is a little strange.

text.traditional: 妳不要緊張，我有辦法，我跟妳一起去。
text.simplified: 你不要紧张，我有办法，我跟你一起去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǒu bànfǎ, wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
text.english: Don’t be nervous. I have an idea: I can be there for you.

text.traditional: 太好了，謝謝妳幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 太好了，谢谢你帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, xièxie nǐ bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: Great! Thank you for helping me.

text.traditional: 不客氣。妳打算什麼時候跟他見面？
text.simplified: 不客气。你打算什么时候跟他见面？
text.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou gēn tā jiànmiàn?
text.english: You’re welcome. When do you plan to meet him?

text.traditional: 可能這個週末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他約時間。
text.simplified: 可能这个周末吧。如果你有空，我再跟他约时间。
text.pinyin: Kěnéng zhège zhōumò ba. Rúguǒ nǐ yǒukòng, wǒ zài gēn tā yuē shíjiān.
text.english: Maybe this weekend. If you are free, I will arrange a time with him.

text.traditional: 有空啊，但是我明天不會來學校，等妳決定了，再給我打電話吧。
text.simplified: 有空啊，但是我明天不会来学校，等你决定了，再给我打电话吧。
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng a, dànshì wǒ míngtiān bú huì lái xuéxiào, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà ba.
text.english: I am free, but I won’t come to school tomorrow. When you decide, call me.
